items.text: Time seems to be frozen in the utility room.
The sound of breathing is the only sign of its passage.
Staring at the pile of letters between them, both Vila and Name Day realize that their problems demand answers.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrade Windsong did not say whether it was a good idea to return.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: As I just asked ...

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Would you consider staying here, even after knowing what was in this letter?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: See, your question shows you don't think the truth will stop me.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Looks like neither of us have changed our minds.
Vila shakes her head, taking the letter off the typewriter.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You know I'm still going, and I know you'd prefer for us to stay here.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Alright. Since you know the truth, I won't keep it from you any further.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Are you setting off tomorrow?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: If possible, sure. We've waited for too long—Too long not to know.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: All I want is a chance to see it with my own eyes.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: I'll try my best to ...

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: *sigh* Remember I told you what happened that day when the "Storm" fell? That Avgust went out alone to take a look.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I remember. But back then, I didn't know much about the "Storm," less even than what I know now.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I thought he just got lost.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I had no idea what he might have seen.
Vila looks to Avgust, who is taking each letter from its envelope and piling them up.
Their different layers, one after another, begin to resemble, at least in the mind of Avgust, a layered cake.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: A Napoleon Cake!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Look, Vila!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Thank you for the cake, but did you forget what I said, Comrade Avgust?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Don't go out alone.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But since you're here for these "eternal souls," I think we can help.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But I didn't leave my comrades!
He points at the door. They see the edge of some clothes hidden behind the door frame, accompanied by grouchy whispers.
Don't push me—I can't hear anything!
What do you expect? Comrade Avgust just sold us out!
Let's just go in already!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I had no idea we had so many listeners.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Come out, all of you. Pyotr, Pasono, Nina, and anyone else you've got with you too!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I have something that I must tell you.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Vila ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I know what you want to ask, and yes, we're going home.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And if all goes well ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We will be going home tomorrow.
The hard-packed snow crunches under the weight of feet, big and little, as the team led by Vila inch close to home once again.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Why didn't we come home from the pier?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Turtles in the sea place their houses there and then go on shore.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We're not going home for good, Comrade Avgust.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is just ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: A visit.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Just like the ones Comrade Windsong used to make, remember?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then are we guests? Does that mean we stay in the hotel tonight? But there are still houses for us, right?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I can't see the pier or the statue from here.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: All the rooftops and the snow become one. The snow has covered everything.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We're here ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: ... because this is the best place to see all of Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I see nothing. No pier. No statue.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They're gone.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Both sea foam and snow all eventually vanish.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vanish, is that the word?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I don't know.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: There are a lot of questions that I can't answer.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Besides, I'm not always right.
Avgust falls deep into his own mind, but Nina cautiously takes Vila's hand and asks her in a trembling voice.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Vila, wasn't the mine on our way home?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: But this doesn't look like the way home anymore.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: It's strange.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: I just want to see mama again, and then we can go back to the SPDM with Pasono.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Vila, is this really Rayashki?
Vila holds her hand even tighter. This time, she doesn't bend down to wipe the tears from the little girl's face.
There is no soft word of comfort left in her, only hard truth.
There was a path from here down to the town. During snowy days, people would tie red tape on the trees to mark the way home.
But now she sees only white, no colors at all except the sunlight reflecting on the snow.
The road home is gone.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is still Rayashki.
A moment later, she turns around.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Let's go, children.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It's getting cold out. It's time to go back.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Is the visit over, Vila?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Yes. It's over.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Madam ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Name Day.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Just as we agreed yesterday ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I will join the Foundation.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: You're more than welcome! But, please, if you need, you can spend some more time here.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Thank you. That's thoughtful of you.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But it won't be necessary.
